newsitem.title: USA: Texas separatists given police ultimatum.
newsitem.headline: Texas separatists given police ultimatum.

text.p: The Texas separatists holed up in a mountain compound were given an ultimatum late on Thursday night to surrender or risk forced arrest by scores of police surrounding them, officials said.

A state government spokesman and the attorney for the Republic of Texas leader Richard McLaren said police negotiators had made their final offer in a five-day standoff and that he should respond quickly.

"It is now in his court to respond to this," said Mike Cox, spokesman for the Texas Department of Public Safety. He declined to give details of the offer and did not say how long McLaren had to respond.
McLaren's attorney Terence O'Rourke said he had advised his client "in no uncertain terms to end it."
"I as a lawyer for Richard McLaren and his friends have made the best deal I can: a final written offer and it is a final written offer," O'Rourke told reporters late Thursday.
McLaren, 43, and 12 other Republic members, who believe Texas is an independent nation, have been surrounded by elite police units in their West Texas mountain compound since Sunday.
O'Rourke said police had decided to force McLaren's hand because increasing numbers of militia members allied with McLaren's group had begun to move toward his compound in the Davis Mountains.

"The Texas Rangers and DPS made clear that the rising level of response of armed men is of utmost concern to them," O'Rourke said. "In some respects, this represents a somewhat more dangerous situation than Waco."
In 1993 about 80 Branch Davidian cult members were killed in a huge blaze which consumed their Texas compound at the end of a long siege by FBI agents.
On Wednesday, Texas Rangers in Peco, Texas, 70 miles (112 km) to the north, arrested seven Republic of Texas supporters travelling in two cars loaded guns and ammunition.
Also on Wednesday, two men driving a car with Republic of Texas license plates were stopped just a few miles from the compound and arrested after police found a stolen semi-automatic rifle inside.
O'Rourke said another militia member, armed with a semi-automatic rifle and a semi-automatic pistol, was arrested near the compound on Thursday.

Cox declined to say how much time McLaren had to surrender, but stressed that officials still wanted a peaceful solution to the crisis which began Sunday when Republic members kidnapped two neighbours in retaliation for the arreste of the group's security chief on weapons possession charges.
The hostages were later released, but felony charges were filed against the rebels.
"We have said all along we want a peaceful outcome to this, not a Wild West outcome," said Cox.

The Republic of Texas group, formed in 1995, believes the 1845 annexation of Texas by the United States was illegal. Texas was an independent nation for nine years after breaking away from Mexico in 1836.
